diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout the paper, we let $\mF_t = \sigma(\{\xi_i\}_{i=0}^t)$, for any $t\geq 0$, be the filtration~of~$\sigma$-algebras generated by the sample sequence $\xi_0, \xi_1,\xi_2\ldots$.
At each inner~iteration $j$, we generate a sketching matrix/vector $S_{t,j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times q}\sim S$ for some $q\geq 1$ and solve the subproblem:
Particularly, different directions~may prefer different stepsizes, so that $\baralpha_t$ depends on $\barDelta\bx_t$ and is random.
thus $B_t$ is deterministic conditional on $\bx_t$ (this is why we do not use the notation $\bar{B}_t$)

issues.failure_explanation: The iterate $\bx_t$ is generated using the random sketching matrices $S_{i,j}$ and the random adaptive stepsizes $\bar\alpha_i$, so $\bx_t$ (and hence $\nabla F_t$, $B_t$) is not measurable with respect to $\mF_{t-1}=\sigma(\xi_0,\dots,\xi_{t-1})$ as defined. Consequently $\mE[\bar g_t\mid\mF_{t-1}]$ is $\mF_{t-1}$-measurable while $\nabla F_t$ is not, so the asserted identity in Assumption 2, its analogue in Assumption 3, and the claim that $B_t$ is deterministic given $\bx_t$ are false or ill-posed as written. The same conditioning on $\mF_{t-1}$ is used throughout the proofs (e.g., Lemma aux:lem4(b) and the proofs of Theorem sec3:thm1 and Lemma sec4:lem1), so those steps are formally unjustified until the filtration is enlarged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $\mF_t$ as the sigma-algebra generated by the samples, sketching matrices, and adaptive stepsizes produced up to just before $\xi_{t+1}$ is drawn, and restate all conditioning claims with respect to this enlarged filtration; every identity and proof step then goes through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: All conditional-expectation manipulations in the assumptions and proofs (unbiasedness of $\bar g_t$ and $\bar H_t$, martingale-difference arguments, recursions conditioned on $\mF_{t-1}$) are formally ill-posed as stated; the main-line results inherit this defect in their proofs, although their intended mathematical content is unchanged under the intended (enlarged) filtration.
issues.title: Conditional-expectation identities are false/ill-posed under the stated filtration
issues.why_classification: The defect is a mis-specified sigma-algebra with a one-line, purely notational repair; no bound, rate, regime, or conclusion changes, so every substantive claim and guarantee survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of asymptotic normality is almost identical to the proof of Theorem 5.6 in \cite{Na2022Statistical}.
the stepsize parameters satisfy $\beta\in(0,1)$,~$\chi>\beta$, and $c_{\beta}, c_{\chi}>0$
We~show that all their results still hold, with proofs deferred to Appendix \ref{pf:sec3:subsec2} for completeness.

issues.failure_explanation: The entire proof of Theorem sec3:thm2 consists of citing the proof of Theorem 5.6 in Na2022Statistical and asserting that the weaker, state-dependent growth conditions of Assumptions 2-3 do not affect the normality proof because $\|\bx_t-\bx^\star\|\to0$ almost surely. This reduction is not established: a.s. convergence of the random coefficient in the moment bounds does not by itself supply the uniform moment/integrability control a CLT proof needs (the cited proof assumed bounded fourth moments), and no substitute is supplied or invoked. Moreover, the theorem admits $\beta=1$ (with the $c_\beta$ condition) and requires only $\chi>1.5\beta$, which can be strictly below the $\chi>1$ regime of the cited result, while the only moment bound available in the paper (Lemma sec4:lem1) is restricted to $\beta\in(0,1)$ and is never connected to the normality argument. The transfer of the cited proof to the stated hypotheses is a missing nontrivial step, and the justification given is a non sequitur.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, we only have to note that our growth conditions in Assumptions \ref{ass:2} and \ref{ass:3} on gradients and Hessians do not affect the proof of normality (though they affect the proof of convergence),~since the term $\|\bx_t-\bx^\star\|$ in the growth conditions converges to $0$ almost surely.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry out the CLT argument of the cited Theorem 5.6 under Assumptions 2-4 with $\chi>1.5\beta$, supplying the required moment and uniform-integrability bounds (for $\beta<1$ these can be based on Lemma sec4:lem1); the $\beta=1$ case requires its own moment analysis or exclusion from the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic normality guarantee under the paper's weaker assumptions (in particular for $\beta=1$ and for $\chi\in(1.5\beta,1)$) is unverified; consequently the coverage guarantees of Corollary sec4:cor1 and the online-inference claims built on the normality result rest on an unproven theorem.
issues.title: Proof of the asymptotic normality theorem is not carried out; the claimed reduction to the cited result is unjustified
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained but genuinely nontrivial re-derivation (plus possibly restricting the $\beta=1$ case); it needs no new global proof architecture and a comparable normality result is expected to survive, but as written the proof does not establish the stated theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We point out that $\hat{\Xi}_t$ can also serve as a consistent~covariance estimator for conditioned SGD methods, which follow the update form \eqref{nequ:3} though~$B_t$~may~not approximate the objective Hessian $\nabla^2F_t$.

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw or weaken the claim to state that extending $\hat\Xi_t$ to conditioned SGD requires modifying the analysis (redefining the target covariance through the limiting preconditioner and handling nonsymmetric dynamics), or actually carry out that extension; no formal result supports the claim as written.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised generalization of the covariance estimator to conditioned SGD methods (including AdaGrad, RMSProp, and quasi-Newton methods) is unsupported; consistency of $\hat\Xi_t$ is established only in the unbiased-Hessian (sketched Newton) setting, and the specific assertion about what Theorem sec4:thm1 requires is false.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that the analysis directly applies to conditioned SGD (AdaGrad/RMSProp/quasi-Newton)
issues.why_classification: The only source-supported repair withdraws a substantive advertised scope (consistency for conditioned SGD methods), which exceeds a routine local fix, but it is confined to a discussion claim and leaves all formal results and the sketched-Newton guarantees intact.
